incumbent_comparison: Better than office_chair-v002: the padded back is now divided into visible slate-blue panels, edge piping resolves in the production three-quarter and detail captures, and the full five-wheel base remains clear.

observations.art_direction_fit: The dark slate and blue fabric treatment fits the restrained low-poly furniture palette and preserves the room's original chair colors.
observations.close_up_quality: The production detail capture resolves the chair upholstery sections and keeps the whole chair inside frame.
observations.gameplay_readability: The chair remains visible beside the desk; its RoomDefinition obstacle and dimensions remain independent from the render mesh.
observations.geometric_detail: The captured back shows three distinct fabric panels, piping, a cross seam, and side rails; the profile shows the five spokes, caster wheels, and lift hardware.
observations.material_realism: The slate-blue textured panels separate clearly from the graphite shell and darker frame in the actual RoomScale lighting.
observations.proportion: The padded seat and back feel balanced against the base; the frame remains compact beside the desk.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot measured 20.2 x 41.15 x 16.90 inches; the resolver fits the native candidate to the existing 23 x 44 x 18-inch RoomDefinition envelope.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The real room and close production views show a complete wheeled office chair with a tall back, padded seat, paired arms, central lift, and five casters.
observations.silhouette_quality: The back, seat, arms, lift, and five-star base remain easy to distinguish, with a stronger padded outline than v002.
observations.surface_variation: The seat panels, three back sections, accent piping, metal lift, rubber casters, and shell provide visible material changes.
observations.technical_integration: Godot validation passes with 47 meshes, and the production resolver loads office_chair-v003 as a native local scene across six captures with no fallback.
